title: Drivers of every kind
note: oco-agent welcomes any driver: people get a terminal interface (the board, the journal, the inbox, back to back), the author's phone stays a channel, machines use the command line. Today only an AI driver's client is comfortable; by design all are equal. Begun 2026-11-12: the command line any driver can type (oco-agent beat | submit | release | standing | next), answers in plain words. Still to come: the terminal interface for people, and the phone. 2026-11-12: a driver anywhere can now ask, beat, see where things stand, read a job's log and wait for it, through the repository alone (--via). 2026-11-12: drivers can say things to one another, and the author is reached on the phone by oco-agent itself (say, inbox, ntfy as the adapter).

title: A job's header counts only at the top
note: Found 2026-11-12: submit removes every line beginning with '# lab:' anywhere in a script, so a script that carries other text (a workflow, a heredoc) loses lines silently. Only the header's own place - after the shebang - should count. oco-agent's runner must not repeat this.

title: Investigate: the agent stopped starting jobs (2026-11-11, 22:29 CET)
note: The machine was on. The agent started its last job at 22:29:23 CET (while a 21-repository rollout begun at 22:28:30 was still running) and logged nothing more until the author rebooted at 23:14:31, although a job waited from 22:45. The author had unplugged the phone at 22:22 - a clue: some of the lab watches the phone. After the reboot (lingering on) the agent ran but picked up nothing new for about 20 minutes - most likely replaying old jobs, see replay-never. The journals of both boots are on the machine. 2026-11-12: probable cause found - a GitHub request with no time limit (see the research). The phone was unplugged again at 03:06 on 2026-11-12 with both agents serving on; nothing stalled. Cause of the replays proven 2026-11-12 (see the research): a listing that silently stops at 1,000. lab-agent's daemon is stopped and disabled until fixed.

title: lab-agent: read what is done without a silent limit
note: already_handled lists the results folder with the contents API (at most 1,000 entries, silently). Read it from the git tree, which says when it is cut short, and refuse to run anything from a listing that is not whole. Until then lab-agent's daemon stays disabled: it would replay again at its next start. It also carries the author's notifications, so this comes before its voice returns. 2026-11-12: built - every listing lab-agent makes (its jobs folder, its results folder) is read from the git tree and refused if cut short; every request has connect and read limits; a test proves a cut-short listing is an error. NEXT: release it, look for jobs that never ran (they would run late, lab-agent has no start-by), then let its daemon serve again for the author's voice. DONE 2026-11-12: lab-agent 0.1.53 released and serving on the lab (installed for the user, checksum checked; the packaged 0.1.52 until sudo pacman -Syu). Its first words: '1135 job(s) already have results' - the whole listing - and it started nothing.

title: A failing run after a merge must be heard
note: 2026-11-12: from the moment oco-agent's crates joined lab-agent's workspace, every Release run on main failed (release-plz looked for the new crates at lab-agent's tags) and nothing said so - land waits on a pull request's checks, not on what runs after the merge. land should wait for the runs a merge starts, or the observatory should show a failing main as loudly as a failing pull request. Fixed for now by giving oco-agent's crates their own tag names.

title: A reconnect never replays finished jobs
note: 2026-11-11 23:34: after lab-agent connect (max jobs given as 50), the agent re-ran the session's old jobs - it could not see their results - fifty at a time, on the same repository clones; the author stopped it within minutes. Two replayed pin updates opened pull requests (both legitimate tad 0.4.0 bumps). 1002 jobs were moved to archive/2026-11-11 in the jobs repository and max_parallel set back to 1. A job must run once: the agent keeps its own record of jobs started, never runs a job older than itself unless asked, and connect never resets that. Proven in oco-agent's rules (2026-11-12): run once by construction, and the 2026-11-11 log replayed refuses all 102. Still open until oco-agent, not lab-agent, is the one running jobs.
waits_on: lab-agent's daemon retiring: oco-agent cannot replay, lab-agent 0.1.53 reads listings whole

title: Something that notices when the watcher stops
note: The watcher's schedule failed silently for hours on 2026-11-12. A second, independent clock should notice when it stops: a dead man's switch outside GitHub (Healthchecks, which can alert through ntfy) pinged by every watcher run. Needs an account the author creates. 2026-11-12: GitHub's schedules did not fire for the watcher at all; the pulse (decision 2026-11-12-the-pulse) is built into oco-agent and waits only for its address: the author creates a free Healthchecks.io check (period 15 min, grace 30 min) with an ntfy integration to the urgent topic, and puts the check's ping address in ~/.config/oco-agent/pulse-url on the lab (mode 600). DONE 2026-11-12: the pulse lives. A check 'the lab: oco-agent pulse' on Healthchecks.io (period 15 min, grace 30 min) receives oco-agent's pulse every five minutes; its address is a private file on the lab (~/.config/oco-agent/pulse-url, mode 600). Alerts go to the account's email; the author adds an ntfy integration for the urgent topic in Healthchecks' web page. Healthchecks is one adapter: any dead man's switch that takes a request at an address will do, its own self-hosted server included.
